A recombinant human complement C1 esterase inhibitor (rh C1INH) is under investigation. ◊ Complement C1 esterase inhibitor may be effective in both the prevention and treatment of acute hereditary angioedema.1 It has also been tried in the management of other conditions including sepsis (see Septicaemia, p.190) and capillary leak syndrome.2 It is under investigation for the treatment of pancreatitis and for use in allogeneic lung transplantation, thermal injury, and shock.2 It is also being studied as a means of limiting reperfusion injury in patients with acute myocardial infarction.3 1.
